questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have been wanting to study in the Netherlands for a long time, so I had no doubts that this was my first priority. This is partially due to the language, as the Dutch usually speak English on a high level. Other than that I had heard many positive things about their educational systems, which was also a crucial aspect for me when choosing this as my study destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Luckily I had prepared a lot from home which definitely helped a lot. Also, on the university's website, they had several guidelines in order to help upon arrival which I used a lot and found to be a great help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I signed up for a buddy programme, to have a local show me around the city. I also joined several intro-events and their "One-stop-shops" which helped students getting a chipcard, setting up a bank account etc. That was really helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was definitely not easy. I eventually had to move 4 times to different AirBnb's.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That they have to prepare in very good time. All the on-campus accommodations were already fully booked for the year way before I even got my acceptance letter from the Uni. And the accommodations in the city are pretty expensive, so it definitely takes some time finding affordable housing that isn't too far away.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to contact the coordinator and send him my requests for the different courses I would like to take, and he registered for me.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The coordinator was definitely the greatest help and all the help I really needed. I forwarded all my questions to him.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I would say successful. I was pretty early about sending my desired courses, so I got the ones I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared in good time, first of all! Also, due to covid some of the courses' timetables were changed after registration had ended - which I had some difficulties with since I experienced some overlaps between exam dates. So double-check that the timetables for your desired courses do not overlap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level of courses changed a lot from course to course. Some I was shocked about "only" having 5 ECTS given the level and the reading burden, where other courses were more doable.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was a big difference. First of all the block structure is shorter, so there are exams every 2 months instead of twice a year as in UCPH. For me, that meant I still had to get the same amount of ECTS (30) as in my home university's semester-structure, but in shorter time. Also, at UCPH there is no mandatory attendance, nor do you get graded on participation in class. Due to this, on UCPH the style of teaching is more relaxed and made (for me) a better and safer environment to participate voluntarily in the class discussion without having to worry about saying the wrong thing and getting a bad grade thereafter. That was probably the hardest thing for me to get used to at Erasmus University in Rotterdam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Research and Writing Skills (Arbitration skills), Corporate and White-collar crime and governance, Mediation Advocay and Legal theory and Methods.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Mediation Advocay and Legal theory and Methods.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Housing was more expensive than I expected and cheap accommodations were very hard to come by.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transportation is very expensive in the Netherlands, so I'd recommend renting a bike. For example from Swapfiets which is approx. 100 kr. pr. month.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were multiple sports clubs you could join as well as a fitness center on campus. Apart from that a lot of opportunities to join different social clubs as well.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join either a social club or the ESN. It is a great way to meet people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the beach at Den Haag in the summer, check out the architecture in Utrect and do a weekend trip to Amsterdam.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I thought it was fairly easy. The Netherlands and Denmark are quite similar in many ways.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to local clubs, parks etc., and try to learn just a few phrases in Dutch. It will take you very far and they always receive you with a positive mindset.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not really experience any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Definitely the people as Dutch people are very friendly. Also, there are a lot of cultural things to discover.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Prepare for accommodation in very good time!! Rent a bike to save money on public transportation. Don't spend money on Erasmus' "Eureka-week" as I found it to be more for the new Dutch students and not the international students as much. I'd recommend doing the ESN intro days instead.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It can be a good idea to set up a Dutch bank account as credit cards/visa are not broadly accepted everywhere.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people from different places around the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to another school system.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Sometimes it can be overwhelming but in the end its super rewarding to go on an exchange and I'd recommend it to anyone!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
